scope: Theorem 4.4 (The threshold trace is the volume extension) of the manuscript “B-semiampleness for compact log-smooth Kähler fibrations” (preprints/B-semiampleness-for-compact-log-smooth-Kahler-fibrations-September-10-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 033 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 afad4b593eede2dd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In the setup of (4.1), choose locally a frame s of OS(mQS), and let τ be its tautological root as in Section 3.1. For every prime P ⊂ S, ordHdg P (τ) = tP − 1. (4.6) More precisely, let π : e V → V be a coordinate power chart making the local pure variation unipotent, and let Eχ be its extended highest eigenline. For a sufficiently divisible positive integer a, the open identification s⊗a ↔ τ⊗am extends to an isomorphism of actual bundles π∗ OS(amMS)|e V ≃ E ⊗am χ . (4.7) One integer a suffices on the compact base. The resulting extension rule commutes with pullback to disks generically meeting U, after further power substitution on the disk. All assertions allow arbitrary rational coefficients on the vertical components of DW .
